Items.Authors: Woong-Seob Jeong, Youngsoo Jo, Yujin Yang, Myung Sang Huh, Gil Jae Lee, Jeonghyun Pyo
Items.Title: Fabrication and evaluation of aluminum image slicers for high-throughput IFU spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We present the development and of aluminum image slicers intended for use in astronomical spectrographs. The image slicer is fabricated from aluminum materials using a diamond-turning machine equipped with customized end mills. Machining parameters were optimized through test cuts on aluminum materials, establishing stable mirror-finish conditions with an average surface roughness of ~10 nm. After optimization for prototype slicers, we achieved average surface roughness values of 10-13 nm, demonstrating reproducible smooth surfaces over the full array of slicer facets. These results confirm that direct diamond-turning machining of RSA6061 can meet the surface quality required for high-throughput, low-scatter reflective image slicers. We outline the planned integration of the fabricated image slicer into a prototype Integral-Field-Unit (IFU) spectrograph and discuss the expected improvement in observing efficiency for future ground-based and space-based instruments.

Items.Authors: Ceiwynn C. Longworth, Megan M. Delamer, Suvrath Mahadevan, Joe P. Ninan, Kathleen Gehoski, Krushna Jadhav
Items.Title: Fabrication of focusing optics for TA-MOONS: Micro-MOONS
Items.Abstract: Tackling open problems in star formation requires precise spectroscopic observations of a large number of young stellar objects, spanning a wide wavelength band from the optical through the near-infrared. The TIFR-ARIES Multi-Object Optical to Near-infrared Spectrometer (TA-MOONS) is a new astronomical instrument designed to survey young stars. To precisely position starlight into its 8 robotic arms, an array of microscopic, concave mirrors is needed. The fabrication of the mirror array called Micro-MOONS was done using two-photon polymerization 3D printing. The mirrors are created of IP-S photoresist on a silicon substrate, with fabrication focusing on uniformity, minimizing surface roughness, and preserving the desired curvature radius.

Items.Authors: Cecilia R. Fasano, Chi C. Cheung, Marc Christophersen
Items.Title: Fabrication of near-UV multilevel diffractive lenses using grayscale E-beam lithography and TASTE
Items.Abstract: Advancements in the technologies used to observe the Ultraviolet (UV) bandpass (900-4000 Å) are necessary to enable the next generation of UV observatories. Optical components, including gratings and lenses, used in UV instruments can be improved via advanced techniques developed for the semiconductor fabrication industry. In particular, the evolution of grayscale lithography enables the creation of more complex 3D structures at micron- to nanometer-length scales. We report on efforts to use grayscale electron beam lithography (EBL) in combination with thermally activated selective topography equilibration (TASTE) to fabricate multilevel diffractive lenses (MDLs) in poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) for use in the near-UV where PMMA exhibits high transmission.     This work was supported by the Office of Naval Research.   Distribution Statement A. Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

Items.Authors: Imke Ottersberg, Viljon Sekseni, Kersten Mumme, Freerk Schütt, Dhruti Mavani, Lakshay Rajput, Miriam Brandt, Philipp Huke
Items.Title: Fast-controlled fiber-telescope interface for astrophysics
Items.Abstract: Small-scale telescopes connected with fibers allow the use of small-scale high-resolution spectrographs. This is interesting for telescopes with diameter even below one meter. Combining multiple telescopes is even more interesting as it allows to get a large amount of photons at a low cost. The CREOL-group demonstrated the capacity of a fiber-connected multi-telescope approach. Fiber-connected telescopes require demanding accurate alignment of the starlight in the focal plane. While at large telescope the tip-tilt control suffices smaller telescopes have to be adjusted themselves.  We present here a solution based on a fast control loop (up to 100Hz) that allows the accurate positioning of the fiber in the focal plane. A fiber-bundle with 19 fibers is used with the central fiber feeding the spectrograph. Light from the targeted star that enters the surrounding control-fibers is detected. The fast positioning is realized by a piezostage while for slow movements the telescope is adjusted

Items.Authors: James McKevitt, Duncan Rust, Berend Winter, David Walton, Sarah Matthews, Ted Pyne, Yukio Katsukawa, Ryohko Ishikawa, Alexey Shitvov, Chloe Wishart, Barry Whiteside, Jacob Parker, Diagarajen Carpanen
Items.Title: Filter and baffle design for the short-wavelength camera on SOLAR-C EUVST
Items.Abstract: SOLAR-C, which is scheduled to launch in the late 2020s with the Extreme Ultraviolet High-Throughput Spectroscopic Telescope (EUVST), will deliver EUV spectroscopy of the solar atmosphere with unprecedented temperature coverage and resolution. We present the optical design and mechanical impacts for the short-wavelength camera, and how our design choices affect scientific performance using complete forward modelling. We discuss the design and optical impact of the thin-film aluminium filter and supporting mesh, including diffraction and shadowing effects in spectral and spatial dimensions. We analyse this using our own Fourier optics method and analytical modelling, and quantify the scientific impact using forward modelling driven by a simulated solar atmosphere. We address the vulnerability of thin-film filters during launch depressurisation using vacuum chamber testing. We describe the stray-light baffle design and low-scatter coatings which suppress visible stray light.

Items.Authors: Alexia Landry, E J Zinat Sathi, Julia Bryant, Heike Ebendorff-Heidepriem, Yunle Wei
Items.Title: First hexabundle optical fibre imaging bundles for the infrared
Items.Abstract: After the success of optical fibre imaging bundles “hexabundles”, for IFS on telescopes such as the Anglo-Australian telescope, there is a desire for hexabundles that work in the near-infrared for use on large wide-field telescopes. New hexabundles being developed at Astralis-USyd are the first hexabundles for astronomy in the near-infrared with optical performance suitable for next generation telescopes. Until recent developments, hexabundles made of infrared optical fibre, ZBLAN, would have been impossible due to the performance and fragile nature of the material. However substantial improvements to the ZBLAN preform at Adelaide University have enabled a more robust fibre that may make infrared hexabundles viable. We will present throughput and Focal Ratio Degradation (FRD) performance of the newly improved ZBLAN fibres and initial infrared hexabundles.

Items.Authors: Zhengqi Sun
Items.Title: Flatness optimization strategy for cryogenic MOSAIC focal plane arrays: a finite element analysis and shim-based compensation method
Items.Abstract: This paper proposes a flatness optimization method for a cryogenic 4×4 GSENSE1517BSI sCMOS mosaic array. Addressing the challenge of thermo-mechanical deformation in SiC-packaged sensors mounted on Invar backplates, we utilize Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to predict surface warping caused by cooling to -40°C and gravity loads. We introduce a quantitative compensation algorithm that leverages the sensor's 3-point mounting interface to calculate optimal shim thicknesses for room-temperature assembly. The results demonstrate that this predictive compensation strategy effectively neutralizes thermal shrinkage and manufacturing tolerances, ensuring superior co-planarity for high-precision scientific imaging.

Items.Authors: Edoardo Alaimo, Fabio D'Anca, Daniele Spiga, Ugo Lo Cicero, Michela Todaro, Luisa Sciortino, Federico Fiorentino, Fabio Reale, Gabriele Cozzo, Pekka T. Törmä, Bahawal Haq, Bart De Pontieu, Paul Boerner, Peter Cheimets, Ken McCracken, Daniele Brienza, Denise Perrone, Marco Stangalini, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: Flight-oriented design reconfiguration and diffractive effects analysis of CNT-based entrance filters for the MUSE EUV spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The NASA MUSE mission is developed to target key astrophysical questions about the solar corona with its first-ever high-resolution, both in time and in angle, EUV spectroscopy images; thus, diffraction impacts due to the entrance optical blocking filters (OBFs) must be thoroughly studied. We present flight-oriented updates to the MUSE entrance CNT-based OBFs proposed after the results of mechanical vibration tests performed on Structural/Thermal-Model filters. While they resisted qualification loads, higher-stress tests showed partial failure due to excessive dynamic differential pressure. A metal honeycomb supporting structure replacing the finer CNT-based mesh, and a thicker CNT-membrane used to increase, robustness are employed. Initial simulations indicate negligible diffraction relative to the PSF core at detector resolution, and also reduced intensity of secondary-order lobes compared to earlier designs. Updated core-PSF throughput estimates are compared to heritage solutions.

Items.Authors: Maxime Rombach, Jean-David Perriard, Laurent Chevalley, Markus Thurneysen, Diane Chapuis, Jean-Paul Kneib
Items.Title: Focal plate prototyping for modular focal planes of stage-5 instruments for ground-based telescopes
Items.Abstract: Focal plate structures for Stage-5 instruments are a central part of the focus and tolerance chain of the optical fibers positionning. Prototyping such structures is therefore critical in the development of the next generation of highly multiplexed instruments.  This paper presents the manufacturing and measurements processes of a prototype of such a plate.

Items.Authors: Tyrone Woods, Patrick Côté, John S. Pazder, Matthew A. Taylor
Items.Title: FORECASTOR: getting ready for the next generation flagship UV space telescope
Items.Abstract: The Cosmological Advanced Survey Telescope for Optical and ultraviolet Research (CASTOR) will provide an essential bridge in the post-Hubble era, preventing a protracted UV-optical gap in space astronomy, and enabling an enormous range of discovery opportunities from the solar system to the nature of the Cosmos. FORECASTOR (Finding Optics Requirements and Exposure times for CASTOR) will supply a coordinated suite of mission-planning tools that will serve as the one-stop shop for proposal preparation, data reduction, and analysis for the CASTOR mission in an open-source and user-friendly format. In this talk, I'll present the latest results of this effort, including photometric and spectroscopic exposure time calculators, image simulation tools for galactic and resolved stellar populations, and survey scheduling tools, and provide illustrative science cases illustrating their use and the unprecedented capabilities of the CASTOR mission.

Items.Authors: Zou Xusheng, Guifeng Chen, Yonggang Gu, Zhen Zhang
Items.Title: FPGA-accelerated fiber optic position detection
Items.Abstract: The current LAMOST（Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope）system employs high-resolution cameras with numerous fibers requiring detection and positioning. However, the host computer's processing speed is inadequate, causing each fiber image analysis to take over ten seconds, which significantly hinders rapid fiber positioning and control. To address the need for rapid and precise positioning of massive fiber spots in high-resolution images, this paper proposes a FPGA-based parallelized algorithm for spot center extraction. A new run-length encoding recognition algorithm for connected domain design is developed, incorporating label removal and equivalence table mechanisms to significantly reduce resource consumption. Through a parallel pipeline processing architecture, the system achieves high-speed image acquisition and sub-pixel-level spot center localization.

Items.Authors: Aurélie Magniez, Peter Wizinowich, Robert J. Harris, Tim Morris, Emily Ronson
Items.Title: From glass to print: 3D printed pyramids as wavefront sensors
Items.Abstract: Pyramid wavefront sensors (PWFS) are central to the next generation of high-contrast astronomical adaptive optics (AO) systems thanks to their high sensitivity. Current challenges associated with the manufacture of 4-facet glass pyramids or pairs of roof prisms include the difficulty and cost of achieving the requirements on flatness, edge-sharpness and achromaticity. These constraints limit design flexibility and restrict deployment of high-performance PWFS in current and future instruments.    High-precision 3D optical printing offers a promising alternative. Polymer-based additive fabrication enables compact, low-cost components with sub-micron surface accuracy, custom apex geometries, and thicknesses far smaller than achievable in glass. This work presents the first fabrication, testing on the POPY bench and analysis of 3D-printed pyramids for PWFS, including inverted designs and integrated spatial-filtering features impossible to realize using conventional optics.

Items.Authors: Markus Feldt, Thomas Bertram, Falk Eilenberger, Camille Graf, Pascal Jaufmann, Maud Langlois, Andreas Obereder, Raphael Pourcelot, Silvia Scheithauer, Horst Steuer
Items.Title: From METIS towards PCS: sequential closed-loop operation of a hybrid pyramid-Zernike sensor for extreme AO at the ELT
Items.Abstract: Both the Zernike and the pyramid wavefront sensor belong to the class of Fourier filtering sensors. Yet they vary greatly in terms of dynamic range, linearity, and sensitivity. The classical solution when both is needed is to operate these two (or similar) sensors in a dual-stage system, where the Zernike sensor would be located downstream of the pyramid.    A more cost-effective approach would be to devise a hybrid concept that can operate as one or the other, in temporally sequential order. So-called meta materials enable the creation of focal-plane phase masks for Fourier filtering sensors, which were only possible in computer simulations until recently.     We will present simulation results regarding the switch-over phase between the two concepts, and regarding the challenges resulting from controlling a single, high-precision, low dynamic range sensor in dual-stage closed loop. In addition, we will show initial ideas for realizing a corresponding phase plate.

Items.Authors: Janina Krieg, Eva-Christina Mischke, Volker Seibert, Ralf Jedamzik, Thomas Westerhoff
Items.Title: Fused, closed-back ZERODUR mirror substrates: meeting the stringent requirements of ELT M5-like mirrors
Items.Abstract: ZERODUR® glass-ceramic is renowned for its near-zero thermal expansion, making it a leading choice for high-precision mirror substrates in astronomy and space missions. SCHOTT’s innovative adhesive-free fusing technology for closed-back, lightweight ZERODUR® mirrors aims to meet stringent requirements for weight, stiffness, and thermal stability, such as for ESO’s ELT M5-like mirrors. This work presents FEM analysis results demonstrating the potential of these fused substrates to deliver the needed performance in advanced optical applications.

Items.Authors: Matteo Colombo, Glen Douglass, David Sweeney, Barnaby Norris, Peter Tuthill, Simon Gross, Olivier Guyon
Items.Title: GLINT: characterization of achromatic phase shifters for broadband photonic nulling interferometry
Items.Abstract: Photonic technologies currently adopted in astronomy suffer from narrowband operation, whereas broad bandwidth achromatic behaviour is mandatory to maximise throughput and efficiency. Current photonics instruments have tackled this challenge by employing passive approaches, with active controls restricted to global delay modulation. But their performance is still limited by unavoidable wavelength-dependent phase errors introduced during fabrication, highlighting the need for active mechanisms to compensate for them. In this work, we characterize different passive devices to understand their chromaticity, with the goal to restore photonic devices’ intended broadband achromatic behaviour. We also explore the use of tunable achromatic phase shifters to sculpt arbitrary dispersion relations. These devices have direct relevance for current and future instruments, where precisely tuned chromatic performance is essential for starlight suppression and exoplanet characterisation

Items.Authors: Gaetano Sivo, Celia Blain, Masen Lamb, Martin Tschimmel, Andreas Seifahrt, Tim Gaggstatter, Joseph D'Amato, Julia Scharwächter, Ricardo Cardenes, Jed Diller, Pedro Gigoux, Heather Carr, Logan Sato, Thomas Schneider, Christine Ricardo, Christophe Clergeon, Stan Karewicz, Elka Koehler, Ruben Diaz, Vincent Garrel, Thomas Hayward, Stephen Goodsell, Scott Dahm, Andrew Adamson, Emanuele Piersanti, Marco Girardini, Giulia Tollero, Jonathon S. Lawrence, Yizheng Wang, Michael Goodwin, Benoît Neichel, Thierry Fusco, Julien Charton, Carlos Correia, Pierre Jouve, Sylvain Cetre, Andrew Rakich, Jessica Zheng, Christopher Coote, Summer Luo, Tomothy Chin, Zhemin Cai, Ali Ghari Zadeh, Dani Guzman, Helen McGregor, Anne-Sophie Bruni-Favier, Delphine Barbon-Dubosc, Tony J. Farrell, Lewis Waller, Julie Magri, Daniel Kerley, Edward L. Chapin, Jean-Pierre Veran, Suresh Sivanandam, Uriel Conod, Adam Muzzin, Nelson Nunes
Items.Title: GNAO: the new AO facility for Gemini North: moving towards the AIV phase
Items.Abstract: The next-generation Gemini North Adaptive Optics (GNAO) project will position the Gemini North telescope as a premier high-spatial-resolution facility for survey science and transient follow-up in the rapidly evolving landscape of astronomical facilities. GNAO will use four laser guide stars to provide the Gemini North telescope with a state-of-the-art wide-field AO facility for observations at near-infrared wavelengths. GNAO is designed to be fully integrated into the Gemini queue scheduling. The f/32 output beam of GNAO is optimized to feed GIRMOS (Gemini Infrared Multi-Object Spectrograph) offering multiplexed integral field unit (IFU) spectroscopy with powerful survey capabilities compared to existing single-IFU instruments. In this presentation we report on the progress made during this last design phase and provide updates on our Final Design path forward including details on the AO Bench design, the RTC, the LGS Facility and the Control SW.

Items.Authors: Hu Zou, Zhengyang Li, Min He, Niu Li, Wenxiong Li, Junjie Jin, Kai Xiao, Yunao Xiao
Items.Title: GOTTA prototype telescope and preliminary results from the pilot survey
Items.Abstract: The Global Open Transient Telescope Array (GOTTA) is an ambitious project to build a network of wide-field telescopes. Its goal is to survey the entire optical sky with a 30-minute cadence to a depth of ~21.5 mag. This capability will revolutionize the study of transients by catching rare fast-evolving events and generating high-accuracy light curves. Over the past few years, we have developed a prototype telescope and conducted a six-month pilot survey. This poster introduces the prototype development, commissioning, and data reduction pipeline, and presents some early results. The prototype paves the way for the construction of the full GOTTA array.

Items.Authors: Ann Fitzpatrick, Joseph Mann, Joe Shreeves, Louis Saraff, Vonnie Von Cheng Lau, Carl Geddert, Emma Johnson, Martin Caldwell, Demet Ulusen Aksoy, Tom Wadsworth, Matthew Tildesley, Edgar Castillo-Domínguez, Eduard Muslimov, James Kariuki, Kieran McCall, Liam Boland
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: cryogenic lens mount prototyping – conclusions for the ICAM subsystem
Items.Abstract: The previous baseline design for HARMONI had four near-IR cameras each with 5 lenses. We present the AIT prototyping work and metrology used to characterise the alignment of a representative lens in a mount ring using previously trialled assembly procedure. The achieved alignment is characterised and compared to previous results. Changes to tilt and centration of the optical axis relative to the mount ring in operational conditions (130 K) are discussed and a study to compare the alignment changes due to the effects of temperature and gravity is also presented.

Items.Authors: Johan D. Floriot, Jean-François Sauvage, Zalpha Challita, Quentin Royer, Mélissa Alliguié, Kjetil Dohlen, Bastien Aqua, William Bon, David Le Mignant, Anne Costille
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: prototype developments for the SCAOS object-selection and dichroic exchange modules
Items.Abstract: The HARMONI SCAO (Single-Conjugate Adaptive Optics) operational is enabled by the SCAOS subsystem which consists of a deployable dichroic beam splitter (SDM) and an optical bench including object selection (SOSM), beam control opto-mechanics and the pyramid wavefront sensor.   The SOSM allows the two-dimensional navigation within the 20 arcseconds diameter patrol field of the SCAOS and then to select an off-axis objects.  The SDM is a translation stage that permits to precisely and repeatably position each dichroic plate in the HARMONI optical beam allowing it to reflect blue light to the SCAOS modules while transmitting the red light of the beam to the science spectrograph system.   The current paper presents the qualification characterization performed on prototypes for the SCAOS object selection module (SOSM) and for the dichroic exchange module (SDM).

Items.Authors: Lazar G. Staykov, Tim J. Morris, Deborah Malone, Nazim Bharmal
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: pupil motion tracking and compensation using a wave-front sensor
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a software-based method for the real-time detection and compensation of the pupil motion. By analysing the intensity flux distribution across the wave-front sensor (WFS) sub-apertures, we compute the instantaneous pupil position and distribution and then, if motion is detected, dynamically update the system’s interaction matrix to account for any misalignment in real-time. We examine the performance of this algorithm in various operational conditions, including photon flux, WFS resolution, and wave-front shape and amplitude. Then we compare the results with existing pupil motion compensation techniques and finally discuss the applicability of this algorithm to the HARMONI at the ELT.

Items.Authors: Anne-Laure L. Cheffot, Amita Shrestha, Johannes Prell
Items.Title: Harnessing astronomy knowledge of telescopes to industrialise telescope production
Items.Abstract: In recent years, several publications have suggested that technologies and infrastructure developed for quantum communication could be leveraged to enable long-baseline interferometry. In this article, we provide an overview of the proposed technologies, their current capabilities, and the infrastructure being deployed across Europe. We examine how long-baseline infrared interferometry can benefit from these systems and which adaptations would be necessary to meet its specific requirements.

Items.Authors: Sébastien B. Vievard, Christopher Hamner, Nour Skaf, Michael Bottom, Dylan Hively, Mark Chun, Christoph Baranec, Olivier Guyon, Julien Lozi, Aidan Walk, Josh Corn, Branden Allen, Guillermo Martin, Elsa Huby, Sylvestre Lacour, Manon Lallement, Vincent Déo
Items.Title: He'e-Lab: a modular testbed for astrophotonics and wavefront sensing development
Items.Abstract: Advanced astronomical instrumentation requires accessible platforms to test novel technologies and algorithms. We present the Hawaii Experimental Engineering Lab (He'e-Lab), a modular testbed for wavefront sensing and astrophotonics development. The lab supports: (A) integration and characterization of photonics components in real-time computing environments prior to telescope deployment, and (B) development of wavefront sensing and control algorithms. The testbed features a supercontinuum source (500 nm - 2 μm), a 1k-actuator Boston Micromachines deformable mirror, and downstream instrumentation including photonics injection with a mid-resolution (R~3,000) spectrograph for visible (600-800 nm) wavelengths. Wavefront sensing capabilities include a HASO 126 Shack-Hartmann sensor with planned expansion to emerging technologies. A 37-segment mirror with piston-tip-tilt control enables cophasing research. This platform supports collaborative research, technology development, and education.

Items.Authors: Aaron Omadutt, Roelof S. de Jong, Joe Barrow, Jon Lawrence
Items.Title: High multiplex and precision: the design and development of FLEX, a grid-based fibre positioner with large patrol radius and minimized telecentric error
Items.Abstract: The Fibre Location EXtender (FLEX) is a novel fibre positioner designed to operate within highly constrained focal surfaces in next-generation spectroscopic facilities, such as the Wide-Field Spectroscopic Telescope (which requires 32,000 fibres in a 1.4 m diameter focal surface).  FLEX aims to surpass current available positioner metrics by substantially increasing the fibre patrol radius while minimizing both telecentric error and space between positioners for high multiplex. The patented design uses nitinol (nickel-titanium alloy) in three concentric tubes, maintaining the fibre tip's parallel orientation during tilting. The 110mm-long assembly achieves dense packing with a minimum achievable pitch of ≈5.9mm and a large patrol radius of ≈17mm with a telecentric error of 0.3 degrees when fully extended. Coupled with three piezoelectric actuators, FLEX provides tip, tilt, and piston motion for a large coverage area and vertical refocusing. Initial prototyping results will be presented.

Items.Authors: Maria Vincent, Charlotte E. Guthery, Scott Lilley, Michael Bottom, Sylvain Cetre, Luke Gers, Sonia Karkar, Eduardo Marin, Jonathan Steiner, Johnny Tam, Jacob Taylor, Tatum Umiamaka, Ed Wetherell, Peter Wizinowich, Antonin Bouchez
Items.Title: High order advanced keck adaptive optics (HAKA): results from lab integration and testing of the high order deformable mirror
Items.Abstract: The High Order Advanced Keck Adaptive Optics (HAKA) upgrade will lower residual wavefront error on the Keck II telescope, and enable detailed characterization of older exoplanets, protoplanetary disks, and stars near the Galactic Center. HAKA replaces the original 349-actuator Xinetics deformable mirror with a 2,844-actuator ALPAO magnetic voice-coil DM, upgrades the Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensor, and implements advanced wavefront-control algorithms. The new DM arrived in summer 2025, underwent site-acceptance testing, and some additional tests while integrated with the lab test bench from July 2025 to January 2026. We present the acceptance-test bench design and alignment, closed-loop WFS configuration, and a modular Python control/analysis framework linking the ALPAO SDK to a Zygo interferometer via RPC and interfacing to the real-time controller. Final lab results include DM performance metrics and closed-loop stability demonstrating summit installation readiness.

Items.Authors: Matthias Tecza, Siddharth Maharana, Ryan Griffith
Items.Title: High-dispersion integral field spectropolarimtery: fitting polaristion and spectral orders onto a two-dimensional detector
Items.Abstract: Polarisation of light is a property that tells astronomers much more ddetails about the astrophysics of the objects that their brightness alone. While light from stars is thought to be unpolarised, magnetic fields and light scattering off dust particles, eg in active galactic nucei or atmospheres of exoplanets, imprint a polarisation signature that can be used to learn, for example, more about the size and shape of dust particlaes. The polarisation levels are sometimes very small and hence difficult to measure, and typically only a few polarisation instruments exist at observatories. Similarly, high-resolution spectropscopy has many scientific in astronomy but also requires "bright" targets to measure low-velocity kinematic signals or resolve absorption bands of molecules in stellar or planetary atmospheres.

Items.Authors: Uwe D. Zeitner, Martin Heusinger, Thomas Flügel-Paul, Hans Dekker, Matteo Genoni, Martin Rumpel, Tino Benkenstein, Theresia Fernandez Siles
Items.Title: High-efficiency UV transmission gratings for the CUBES spectrograph of the VLT
Items.Abstract: We report on the current state and intermediate results of the realization of the full-size diffraction gratings for the Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph (CUBES) to be installed at ESO’s VLT. The CUBES design is based on two first-order transmission diffraction gratings of line density 3600 l/mm and 3112 l/mm, respectively. The gratings are optimized for peak diffraction efficiency of >95% in the wavelength bands 300…352nm and 346…405nm. Their realization is based on electron-beam lithography, a structure transfer into a fused silica substrate by reactive ion etching, and a fine-tuning of the grating structure by an Atomic-Layer-Deposition process.

Items.Authors: Toshihiro Tsuzuki, Ryoko Ishikawa, Yukio Katsukawa, Yusuke Kawabata, Hirohisa Hara, Masato Yasugaki, Takayoshi Oba, Akie Moritsuka, Sarah Matthews, James McKevitt, Shota Narasaki, Misaki Miyake, Toshifumi Shimizu
Items.Title: High-fidelity stray-light analysis and control for the EUVST instrument on the SOLAR-C mission
Items.Abstract: SOLAR-C is a solar physics mission led by Japan with contributions from the United States and Europe. Its EUV High-Throughput Spectroscopic Telescope (EUVST) performs wide-band EUV spectroscopy, enabling diagnostics from chromospheric temperatures around 10,000 K to 1 MK and up to 15 MK in solar flares. Because EUV emission is faint, suppressing stray light generated inside the instrument is essential to meeting the requirement of less than 1 photons/sec/pix. We developed a high-fidelity stray-light model using a full structural model of EUVST. The model incorporates diffraction-grating BSDF from electromagnetic simulations, measured BRDF for blackened surfaces, PSD-based surface scattering, and particulate contamination scattering tied to cleanliness levels. These improvements enable reliable prediction of the stray light and support the design of baffling, black coating, and contamination-control. This presentation summarizes the analysis approach, model updates, and key findings.

Items.Authors: Peng Chen, Zhengxiang Shen
Items.Title: High-precision ultra-thin glass sheet stacking manufacturing for multi-channel image slicers
Items.Abstract: The Integral Field Spectrometer (IFS) captures three-dimensional spectral data in a single exposure, saving observation time. Using an image slicer, it provides high light throughput, 100% sky coverage, and stable performance in low temperatures, supporting high-sensitivity near-infrared observations. Deployed in the China Space Station Telescope (CSST), the IFS enables high spatial resolution and wide-band spectral observations. The image slicer, composed of 32 sub-slicing facets (0.25mm width), presents manufacturing challenges. This paper proposes an ultra-precision assembly technique using molecular bonding of multi-layer thin glass and an integrated cutting process. A molecular bonding lens error model analyzes errors, improving manufacturing efficiency by eliminating the interference fringe method. Mechanical and thermal tests confirm the facets' surface accuracy and stability, validating the technique's feasibility for meeting CSST-IFS optical requirements.

Items.Authors: Ko Hosokawa, Takayuki Kotani, Hajime Kawahara, Yui Kawashima, Kento Masuda, Aoi Takahashi, Kazuo Yoshioka
Items.Title: High-temperature transmission spectroscopy system for molecular pressure broadening measurements in exoplanetary atmospheric conditions
Items.Abstract: We present a laser-sourced high-temperature transmission spectroscopy system developed to measure the pressure broadening of molecular absorption lines in H₂&He mixtures at proto-solar composition. This platform enables measurements under gaseous exoplanet-like conditions, where temperature- and pressure-dependent broadening parameters remain uncertain in existing molecular databases. The system employs a tunable laser spanning 1525–1630 nm with up to 0.1 pm resolution, coupled through single-mode fiber into a multi-pass Herriott-cell configuration to achieve a 2.5 m effective optical path. A three-zone furnace stabilizes the sealed gas-cell temperatures between 300–1000 K, while photodiodes monitor the transmitted intensity. This acquires spectra with 0.05–0.5% noise and yields CH₄ broadening widths in H₂&He atmospheres differing by ~30% from database values, enhancing analysis of high-dispersion observations. Ongoing upgrade for CO measurements around 2300 nm will also be presented.

Items.Authors: V. S. Dhillon, E. J. Harvey, C. M. Dubbeldam, S. P. Littlefair, M. J. Dyer, S. Dixon, T. Gamble, P. Kerry
Items.Title: HiPERPOL: a polarimetry module for HiPERCAM on the GTC
Items.Abstract: I will present the design of HiPERPOL, a polarimetry module for the quintuple-beam high-speed optical camera HiPERCAM, which is mounted on the 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias on La Palma.

Items.Authors: Lawrence Bissell, Ellie Smith, Ben Buky, David Isherwood, Jay Stephan, David Lee
Items.Title: Hollow cathode lamps: upgrading astronomy’s calibration lamps for the next generation of multi-object spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Wavelength calibration for multi-object spectrographs (MOS) commonly uses hollow-cathode lamps (HCLs). HCLs provide many well-characterised lines in the visible and near infrared. However, these lamps are too faint for future MOS in the VLT/ELT era, due to the large focal planes that must be characterised. This paper presents a technology development project focused on the design and manufacture of a prototype, high-intensity, HCL unit tailored for astronomical purposes. In our custom-built units we are optimizing the cathode design, material, and current, allowing the mosaicking of configurable cathodes. We also present work on characterisation of Cerium cathodes, identified as a potential alternative to Thorium and Uranium due to its favourable nuclear properties. This work provides a roadmap towards robust, scalable calibration solutions for future spectroscopic facilities.

Items.Authors: Davide Giughello, Dhiraj Gupta, Andrea Bianco, Michele Frangiamore, Rita Giuditta Balestra
Items.Title: Holographic photopolymer for astronomical volume phase gratings
Items.Abstract: Spectrographs are essential for understanding many of the fundamental open questions in astronomy. Among their critical components, second only to the detector, is the dispersing element. Since the photopolymers used to fabricate VPH gratings are typically produced by specialized companies, this work introduces a new low-cost photopolymer featuring a simple yet effective formulation. The innovative photopolymer material employs a biocompatible cellulose-based matrix along with other commercially accessible components. In this work, we present its main properties, including diffraction efficiency measurements spanning from visible to infrared wavelengths.  As several new telescopes are planned for the near future, the demand for alternative materials and fabrication techniques for dispersing elements is becoming increasingly critical. This innovative material therefore represents a promising candidate for next-generation VPH gratings.

Items.Authors: Imad Pasha, Roberto Abraham, William P. Bowman, Seery Chen, Steven Janssens, Deborah Lokhorst, Carter Rhea, Lisa Sloan, Pieter van Dokkum
Items.Title: How to guide a telescope array: control of complex differential flexure via the simultaneous use of multiple guiders
Items.Abstract: We present a novel approach for retaining high pointing accuracy with complex telescope systems, applied to the MOTHRA telescope. MOTHRA is an array of 1140 high-end telephoto lenses equipped with tiltable ultra-narrow interference filters. When completed, the system will be optically-equivalent to a 4.7m f/0.08 refractor with an 8 square degree field of view, operating as an R=800 integral field unit. Its line mapping sensitivity will be an order of magnitude deeper than any other facility. MOTHRA leverages a distributed-aperture design, mounting 38 lenses in a honeycomb lattice on each of 30 fork mounts. Distributed aperture telescopes come with unique challenges, one of which is the complex differential flexure patterns imposed by even rigid honeycomb designs. Here we present and characterize a unique approach, using as many as seven independent guiders per mount, all interlaced together, to actively track and compensate for this flexure, producing high quality, stable guiding.

Items.Authors: Dirk Schmidt, Nicolas Gorceix, Thomas Rimmele
Items.Title: Images of the Moon's surface with adaptive optics on the 1.6-meter Goode Solar Telescope
Items.Abstract: We present images of the Moon's surface that we took in visible with adaptive optics on the 1.6-meter Goode Solar Telescope. The use of adaptive optics was possible thanks to a low-light optimized correlating Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor.

Items.Authors: Caleb Cook, Nico Deshler, Logan Pawlowski, Amit Ashok
Items.Title: Imaging sub-diffraction star clusters with spatial mode sorting
Items.Abstract: Passive super-resolution imaging using spatial mode sorting has been vigorously analyzed as a technique to approach fundamental limits of resolution. However, a comprehensive experimental validation of this approach has been limited by the fidelity of hardware implementation of spatial mode sorters in terms of throughput, cross-talk, and spectral bandwidth. The recent availability of high-fidelity MPLC-based spatial mode sorters, such as those from Cailabs, enables a comprehensive experimental validation. In this work, we demonstrate sub-diffraction localization of point emitters, emulating star clusters, in various configurations and different spectral bandwidths. Our experiment employs a hybrid measurement method that combines direct imaging and spatial mode sorting measurements. Our measurement model and image estimation algorithm incorporates various error sources such as shot noise, detector dark current, read noise, residual wavefront error, and pointing error.

Items.Authors: Youngchun Youk, Shinwook Kim
Items.Title: Improved MTF measurement for satellite EO cameras using a multi-bar edge target
Items.Abstract: We propose an MTF measurement method for satellite electro-optical cameras using a multi-bar edge target. In the standard knife-edge approach for linear-detector cameras, the target must be scanned repeatedly to collect enough ESF/LSF samples. During this time, small changes in vibration, temperature, and air flow distort the edge profile and increase run-to-run scatter.  Our target combines multiple edge transitions, so one scan provides MTF estimates from multiple pixel groups. This increases the amount of valid data per target movement and reduces sensitivity to slow environmental drift. In our test setup, the method produced more stable MTF results while shortening the measurement sequence compared with the single-edge target scan.

Items.Authors: Eric J. Grigel, David Adriaanse, Grecia Falcon
Items.Title: Improving observatory resilience: insights from Subaru’s 2024 tropical storm damage
Items.Abstract: In August 2024, the Subaru Telescope on Maunakea, Hawai‘i experienced damage to key exterior systems during a severe tropical storm. The event affected the rotating enclosure weatherseals, the coating system on the fixed structure, and the HVAC chiller exhaust outlets that support thermal control. This paper examines the suspected failure modes that contributed to these issues, with a focus on the environmental stresses experienced during the storm. Methods used for damage assessment, diagnostic testing, and repair planning are described, along with the final proposed repair solutions. The paper concludes with lessons learned intended to support improved design, durability, and resilience for future ground-based observatories in remote locations that experience extreme weather conditions.

Items.Authors: Luisa Sciortino, Michela Todaro, Caterina Tortorici, Federico Fiorentino, Ugo Lo Cicero, Fabio D'Anca, Edoardo Alaimo, Pekka T. Törmä, Bahawal Haq, Pascal Mercère, Paulo da Silva, Fabio Reale, Gabriele Cozzo, Denise Perrone, Daniele Brienza, Marco Stangalini, Alfonso Collura, Salvatore Varisco, Claudio Saitta, Alberto Gulizzi, Gaspare Di Cicca, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: In-band and out-of-band transmission curves of Al/Zr-carbon nanotube FM filters for the Muse mission
Items.Abstract: The NASA Multi-slit Solar Explorer mission, scheduled for launch in 2027, will utilize high-performance optical blocking filters to isolate five critical spectral lines in the 40–120 eV range while attenuating out-of-band solar radiation. This work presents the in-band (EUV) and out-of-band (UV-Vis-IR) characterization of the flight model filter wheel filters for the Spectrograph and Context Imager instruments, fabricated by depositing aluminum and zirconium metallic coatings on carbon nanotube membranes. In-band results show that the thin Zr filters successfully meet the requirements at 10.8 nm, while the thin Al variants show performance at 17.1 nm and 19.5 nm close to the requirements, though failing to meet the 28.4 nm and 30.4 nm thresholds. Out-of-band measurements (190–860 nm) confirm that essentially all the filters comply with the rejection requirement T < 10^-6, validating CNT-based technology for solar space missions.

Items.Authors: Walter Rahmer, Aman Chandra, Zac Chen, Christopher Walker, Daewook Kim
Items.Title: Inflatable primary reflector optical surface simulation and testing
Items.Abstract: Advancing the exploration of astronomical phenomena in the far-infrared band will require larger aperture instruments to enable higher angular resolutions and increased light-collecting ability. Recent developments in inflatable structures offer a promising low mass and volume solution, allowing large concave reflective surfaces to be carried by smaller spacecraft.   This work will leverage related experimental results for membrane structures, presenting a simulation of the aspheric pressure driven reflector shape, a study of a corrective optical design to compensate for the aberrated surface, and recent measured results from a 1-meter test article. Through deflectometry and photogrammetry methods, the optical surface of the test article is evaluated for its geometric sensitivity, repeatability, and shape stability over time. From these results, as well as the current testing campaign, a number of paths for near-term future work are identified.

Items.Authors: Emily Farr, Briana Indhal, Brian Fleming, Kevin France, Dmitry Vorobiev, Fabien Grisé, Nicholas Kruczek, Kristina Davis, Marta Civitani, Davide Sisana, Laura Proserpio, Stefano Basso
Items.Title: Initial optical performance results from the MANTIS SmallSat mission
Items.Abstract: The MANTIS (Monitoring Activity of Nearby sTars with UV Imaging and Spectroscopy) mission is a SmallSat in development at the University of Colorado’s Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics (LASP). Its science payload is built to study high-energy radiation from low-mass host stars and how it shapes the atmospheres of their exoplanets. By observing stellar emission from 100–6000 Å, MANTIS will provide data for understanding radiation-driven atmospheric chemistry and escape. The payload includes two telescopes: a Hetrick-Bowyer grazing-incidence EUV telescope from the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF) and a Cassegrain telescope for simultaneous FUV, NUV, and optical measurements. We present a mission status update, recent progress from the optical test campaign, and efficiency results for the EUV grating, a first-of-its-kind lithographically etched variable-line-spaced grating developed at Pennsylvania State University.

Items.Authors: Gavin B. Dalton, Lucia Suarez, Ellen Schallig, Roberto Martinez, Joel Conception, Kevin Dee, Judith Santos, Neil O'Mahony, Andrea Henderson de la Fuente, Ian J. Lewis, Sarah Hughes, Dario Marante, Don Carlos Abrams, Antonella Vallenari, J Alfonso Lopez Aguerri, Arūnas Kučinskas, Esperanza Carrasco, Scott Trager, Shoko Jin, Chris Benn, Piercarlo Bonifacio
Items.Title: In-situ maintainance and repair techniques for the optical fibres of WEAVE at the primary focus of the William Hershel Telescope
Items.Abstract: WEAVE is a 1000-fibre multi-object spectroscopy facility at the primary focus of the William Herschel Telescope. The nature of the positioner implies that damage to fibres during operations has a reasonably high probability, and thus the instrument was designed with spare length included for each fibre in the system to facilitate repairs. It was originally envisaged that church repairs would require a full dismount of the instrument top-end from the telescope and substantial downtime necessitating return to Cassegrain observations. However, in operations we have developed access to the instrument in useful orientations at the telescope access park position, and have been able to facilitate all envisaged repair activities in-situ without incurring excessive downtime for repairs.

Items.Authors: David Eglin, Miguel Montesinos-Ballester, Davide Pinto, Alessio Cargioli, Lucius Miller, Théa Boussion, Alexei N. Baranov, Roland Teissier, Adrian Glauser, Jérôme Faist, Sascha P. Quanz
Items.Title: Integrated InGaAs/InP waveguides for low-loss astrophotonics between 4-18.5 μm
Items.Abstract: Molecular absorption features make the MIR range interesting, yet compatible photonic technology remains underdeveloped. The planned space mission LIFE could benefit from photonics in place of bulk optics to characterise exoplanet atmospheres at wavelengths between 4-18.5 µm. Lighter, more compact and robust instruments reduce mission complexity, while required throughput, bandwidth, and cryogenic compatibility pose technological challenges. A promising photonic platform is InP/InGaAs with low waveguide (WG) propagation losses reported between 4-11 µm and a broad transparency window. We expand our understanding of this platform by measuring waveguide losses at longer wavelengths and under cryogenic conditions. We report on fabrication, simulation, and loss contributions of InP/InGaAs WGs and present a measurement setup with five lasers emitting between 4 and 16 µm. This lays the foundation for future development of integrated astrophotonic circuits operating at long MIR wavelengths.

Items.Authors: Suresh Sivanandam, Ross Cheriton, Robin Swanson, Ryan Dungee, Mark Barnet, John Weber, Jianhao Zhang, Shurui Wang, Martin Vachon, Pavel Cheben, Dan-Xia Xu, Siegfried Janz, Jens H. Schmid
Items.Title: Integrated photonic adaptive optics for next-generation spectroscopic and interferometric instruments
Items.Abstract: Integrated photonic adaptive optics (AO) offers a new path to diffraction-limited performance by replacing bulk wavefront sensors and deformable mirrors with compact, lithographically defined optical circuits. We present an AO system-on-chip (AOSoC) that uses free-space grating couplers to inject the incident wavefront into a reconfigurable Mach–Zehnder interferometer mesh, which performs both phase sensing and correction with nanometer precision. The corrected beam is coupled into a single-mode fibre or routed directly to an on-chip spectrograph, enabling fully integrated AO-fed instruments. We demonstrate closed-loop operation of a 64-element AOSoC, characterize stability and correction bandwidths. Photonic AO promises compact, low-cost, highly replicable systems for multiplexed spectroscopy, optical interferometry, integrated photonic instrumentation, and free-space optical communication, with on-sky demonstrations now being planned.

Items.Authors: Yunjong Kim, Dohoon Kim, Seonwoo Kim, Sang Hun Lee, Seunghyuk Chang, Jihun Kim, Yeonsik Kim, Il Kweon Moon, Hyuksun Kwon, Woowon Byun, Yongseok Lee, Jaewon Yoo, Kyohoon Ahn, Jae-Woo Kim, Gayoung Lee, Daewook Kim, Jongwan Ko
Items.Title: Integration and performance verification of two K-DRIFT G1: from laboratory alignment to first-light in Chile
Items.Abstract: We present the development and performance verification of two identical K-DRIFT G1 telescopes, designed as 4.43° × 4.43° wide-field off-axis freeform systems for detecting extremely low surface brightness structures. We positioned each freeform mirror using a CMM for initial placement within tolerance. Tolerance analyses identified the secondary mirror as the optimal compensator. Using interferometric measurements and a wavefront-based alignment method, we achieved residual wavefront errors below 120 nm RMS for both telescopes in the lab. Imaging test in the lab showed point spread function performance within 2 pixels across the field, confirmed at the Bohyunsan Optical Astronomy Observatory in Korea. After deployment to the El Sauce Observatory in Chile, both telescopes achieved on-sky image quality within 1.5 pixels, validating their alignment robustness. These results confirm the readiness of the K-DRIFT G1 telescopes for scientific LSB imaging.

Items.Authors: Mercedes Filho, António Amorim, Paulo Garcia, João Canais
Items.Title: Integration, testing, and validation of the cryostat alignment system for the METIS/ELT WSS
Items.Abstract: The WSS subsystem of the METIS first light instrument for the ELT is being manufactured by the Portuguese team of the METIS Consortium. The WSS consists of three units – ELP (elevation platform and main support structure), RIG (staircase and walkway providing access and maintenance) and CAS (movable hexapod that holds the cryostat with the instrument).  Due to its dimensions, the full integration of the WSS with the rest of METIS will only occur in Chile, during commissioning.   In Portugal, the ELP support ring (main ELP support structure) and CAS will be assembled together with a dummy CRY to simulate the mass of the cryostat with the instrument. In this configuration, the assembled structure will be load tested, and the hexapod control movement will be assessed. We here present the strategy to assemble these two units and perform the required testing and validation.

Items.Authors: Vikram Seenivasan, Pradip Gatkine
Items.Title: Inverse-designed tapers to improve throughput of on-chip astrophotonic spectrographs
Items.Abstract: Astrophotonics offers a pathway toward compact, miniaturized, stable spectrographs as their size does not scale with telescope diameter. Thus they offer a cost efficient way to achieve astronomy science requirements. A major limitation of current astrophotonic spectrographs is the loss at interfaces between its distinct components, leading to lower overall throughput. We investigate using inverse design to optimize taper-based transitions between components. Our approach explores two methods of fabrication-constrained inverse design. The first employs shape optimization to modify the boundary geometry of the tapers. The second optimizes a gradient region to gradually transform the optical mode between components. This work demonstrates a pathway toward improving astrophotonic spectrographs using computational inverse design methods. This positions us to design high-performance, cost-effective instrumentation for next-generation large and extremely large telescopes.

Items.Authors: Yusuke Munakata, Tatsuya Sawano, Kanaho Okamoto, Atsushi Takada, Yoshitaka Mizumura
Items.Title: KaGErOFU: design of ground-based gamma-ray burst explorer for optical flash understanding
Items.Abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) occasionally show bright optical flashes during the prompt phase, which can reveal key synchrotron parameters such as the cooling and self-absorption break frequencies. However, these flashes often appear and fade within a few seconds, making them difficult to capture with conventional follow-up observations triggered by satellite alerts.   KaGErOFU (Kanazawa University Gamma-ray Burst Explorer for Optical Flash Understanding) is a multi-platform (ground-based and balloon-borne) wide-field system designed to provide pre-planned, simultaneous optical coverage of GRBs. Using 135-mm f/1.4 lenses and back-illuminated full-frame CMOS sensors, tiled to cover about 3000 deg^2, the system reaches a limiting magnitude of 13.1 in 5-s exposures, sufficient to detect optical counterparts predicted by a power law model for typical Swift/BAT GRBs. We report on the system concept and on ground tests with a prototype camera–mount unit demonstrating imaging capability.

Items.Authors: Zhanshan Wang, Jun Yu, Runze Qi, Chunling He, Zhe Zhang, Pengfeng Sheng, Jingjing Xia, Zhengxiang Shen, Bin Ma, Li Jiang, Chun Xie, Xinbin Cheng, Bitao Wang, Chen Xing, Yulei Wang, Xin Cheng
Items.Title: L5-EUV coronal imager (LECI): optics overview and current status
Items.Abstract: L5-EUV Coronal Imager (LECI) is designed for high-resolution dynamic imaging of the solar corona, enabling reconstruction of the three-dimensional structures and evolutionary dynamics of solar eruptions. In this work, we detail recent progress in the LECI optical system design, mechanical architecture, precision manufacturing and metrology of ultrasmooth mirrors, and the development of EUV multilayer film coatings at the Institute of Precision Optical Engineering (IPOE), Tongji University.

Items.Authors: Aditya R. Sengupta, Benjamin Gerard, Dominic F. Sanchez, Matthew DeMartino, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Michael Messerly, Paul Pax, Daren Dillon, Eric Strang
Items.Title: Laboratory characterization of a multi-photonic lantern optical waveguide using off-axis holography
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns (PLs) are waveguides that convert multi-mode input light to single-mode outputs. Wavefront sensing (WFS) and spectroscopy using a PL have been demonstrated, but PL simulations and experiments show significant mismatches. For the WaveDriver project, a proposed Habitable Worlds Observatory pathfinder that uses a PL for WFS as well as for integral field spectroscopy, we manufactured an optical waveguide consisting of seven 19-port PLs in one device. We present laboratory characterization of the individual PLs, consisting of measurements of the principal modes at each PL input using digital off-axis holography. We compare our mode measurements to simulations to assess the variation in the PL manufacturing process. We discuss expected WFS performance in the WaveDriver configuration. This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under Contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. The document number is LLNL-ABS-2013910.

Items.Authors: Kaining Yang, He Sun, Jiang-Pei Dou, Xi Zhang, Gang Wang, Cheng Yan
Items.Title: Laboratory demonstration of dark hole generation and maintenance on the CPI-C high-contrast imaging testbed
Items.Abstract: The Cool Planet Imaging Coronagraph (CPI-C) on Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope (CSST) combines step-transmission apodized pupil for starlight suppression and a deformable mirror (DM) for wavefront control to suppress the quasi-static speckle noise. In this work, we systematically conducted high-contrast imaging experiments on the CPI-C testbed using Focal Plane Wavefront Sensing and Control (FPWFSC). We used a pairwise probing strategy to estimate the complex electric field in the dark-hole region and computed the DM commands using the Electric Field Conjugation (EFC) algorithm, successfully achieving dark-hole generation and speckle suppression. To mitigate model mismatch in the FPWFSC loop, we further introduced a machine-learning-based model-error correction method and an optimized probe-design strategy, both of which accelerated the convergence of the FPWFSC process. The test results demonstrate that CPI-C achieved a raw contrast on the order of 10⁻⁸ within a working region at angular separations of approximately 4–15 λ/D, and robustly maintained the dark hole under temporally varying aberrations. The contrast can be further improved by introducing a stochastic parallel gradient descent (SPGD) optimization algorithm combining the FPWFSC, which will guarantee the final observational robustness in orbit.
